name: Shealtiel
overview: Shealtiel is a male descendant of the tribe of Levi, known primarily as the father of Zerubbabel according to Ezra 3:2. His role is briefly noted in Scripture without additional personal details or narrative. There are no further notes elaborating on his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Shealtiel means 'I have asked [him] of God [El]; possibly also 'God [El] is a shield' or 'God [El] is a victor.' These meanings reflect a reliance on and trust in God, though the name itself was not given directly by God as a divine designation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Shealtiel as the father of Zerubbabel and as a descendant of Levi. Beyond these relationships, no other family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shealtiel's significance in the biblical narrative lies chiefly in his role as the father of Zerubbabel, a key leader in the post-exilic community. His Levitical heritage situates him within the priestly tribe, underscoring the continuity of God's covenant people through the restoration period. Though not extensively detailed, Shealtiel's mention anchors the genealogical and leadership lines important for understanding God's providence in Israel's history.
